title: The integral dualizing object and its adjunction
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], so $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$. Put $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism of a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $d\ge0$ with $\dim X\le d$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ write $R_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and use ordinary sheaves of modules over these ring sheaves, not a different continuous or condensed coefficient category. Let $Ra_n^!$ be the finite constructible comparison-class exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and put $\omega_{X,n}=Ra_n^!(A_n)_s$.

There is a derived-complete object [def-weil-derived-complete]
$$\omega_{X,R}=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n\omega_{X,n},\qquad\omega_{X,R}\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,n}.$$
Here $\operatorname{Res}_n$ is restriction of scalars along $R_X\to(A_n)_X$, the finite transitions are adjoint to the counit-defined coefficient comparisons, and $R\lim$ is the total right derived inverse limit of a strict realization of that tower [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The object belongs to $D^b_c(X,R)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and every reduction has Tor amplitude in $[-2d,0]$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

For every $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(R)$
$$\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\omega_{X,R})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,R),\qquad C=\Gamma(s,Ra_!K).$$
Here $Ra_!$ is integral compact support [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], sections at $s$ are the coefficient-point functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,L)=R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R\mathcal Hom_{R_X}(K,L))$ is the global derived mapping complex [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Thus $\omega_{X,R}$ represents the right-adjoint value at $R_s$: taking $H^0$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\omega_{X,R})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_!K,R_s)$. This is the value-at-the-coefficient-unit assertion; it does not use existence of an integral exceptional adjoint on arbitrary target inputs.

proof.text: For $m\ge n$ take the isomorphism $u_{m,n}:\omega_{X,m}\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n\to\omega_{X,n}$ of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing], transported to the pro-etale site as its statement specifies. Define $\tau_{m,n}:\omega_{X,m}\to\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}\omega_{X,n}$ as its adjunct under tensor-restriction. The unit and cocycle of that lemma give the unit and cocycle of these transitions. To supply the strict-tower datum required by [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], choose a complex $Q_1$ representing $\omega_{X,1}$. Given $Q_n$, the prescribed morphism $\omega_{X,n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}Q_n$ is represented by a roof $C_{n+1}\leftarrow Q_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}Q_n$ whose left arrow is a quasi-isomorphism, by [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system]. Keep this $Q_{n+1}$ and its right chain map, and define all longer chain transitions by composition. After restriction to $R_X$ these form a strict tower complex realizing every $\tau_{m,n}$. Thus the dualizing objects satisfy exactly the normalization data, not merely an uncategorified list of finite objects.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: coherent finite comparisons make a normalized tower; strictification expanded

proof.text: Apply the total derived inverse-limit functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] to this strict tower and call its value $\omega_{X,R}$. Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] to the normalized tower just constructed. Its canonical counit comparisons are the asserted coherent reduction isomorphisms, and its last sentence gives derived completeness. Functorial K-injective tower resolutions fix the limit comparisons; no canonical cone is inferred from the bare triangulated definition of a derived limit.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: effectivity, displayed reductions and completeness

proof.text: The constant etale input $(A_n)_X$ is locally constant with finite stalks on the single stratum $X$, hence is bounded constructible in degree zero by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. It is flat, with Tor interval $[0,0]$, because tensoring with the coefficient unit is the identity. Its pro-etale counterpart is constructible by [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. Apply [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] to it: $R\mathcal Hom_{A_n}((A_n)_X,\omega_{X,n,\mathrm{et}})=\omega_{X,n,\mathrm{et}}$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}$ with Tor interval $[-2d,0]$, independent of $n$. The equality follows by evaluation at $1$ in the coefficient unit. The dualizing comparison and transport of finite duality in [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] give the same assertions on the pro-etale site. Through step 2 these are precisely the reductions of $\omega_{X,R}$. Taking the test module to be $(A_n)_X$ in the Tor condition also bounds their cohomological supports in $[-2d,0]$. Together with completeness, this checks every condition in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and proves membership and the asserted uniform reduction Tor bound.

source.place: Proof, paragraph 1: constant-input preservation and constructibility

proof.text: Fix $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$. Choose $a\le b$ bounding the cohomology of $K_1$. By [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor] all $K_n$ have Tor amplitude in this same $[a,b]$. Hence [lem-coef-integral-compact-support] applies and gives $N=Ra_!K\in D^b_c(s,R)$ with $N\otimes^L_{R_s}(A_n)_s\cong Ra_{!,n}K_n$. Put $C=\Gamma(s,N)$ and $C_n=\Gamma(s,Ra_{!,n}K_n)$. Applying [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] gives canonical isomorphisms $C\otimes_R^LA_n\cong C_n$. This use of compact-support reduction is justified for every bounded constructible integral $K$, rather than silently assuming finite Tor amplitude in addition.

proof.text:
We will use the following elementary mapping-complex form of scalar adjunction. For a map $u:\mathcal O\to\mathcal S$ of ring sheaves over $R$, ordinary tensor-restriction adjunction is $f\mapsto(x\otimes s\mapsto s f(x))$, inverse $g\mapsto(x\mapsto g(x\otimes1))$. Restriction leaves underlying abelian sheaves, kernels and cokernels unchanged by [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], so it is exact, and derived tensor is everywhere defined by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], so [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] gives $-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}\mathcal S\dashv\operatorname{Res}_u$. The restriction-and-unit map on global derived Hom complexes (formed on the functorial resolutions of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]) induces this bijection on every $H^i$, by [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] applied after shifting the target. It is therefore an isomorphism in $D(R)$:
$$\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal S}(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}\mathcal S,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(K,\operatorname{Res}_uM).$$
Its compatibility with composition and evaluation follows from the unit formula: successive units send $x$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes1$, identified with $x\otimes1$, and successive adjoint evaluations send $(x\otimes s)\otimes v$ to $v s f(x)$. These identities hold on the tensor/Hom complexes before localization, hence on the derived comparisons. The assertion includes ordinary rings and modules by taking the one-object trivial site.

proof.text:
Here is also the elementary limit calculation needed below, for a small ringed site $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ with final object $U$, an $R$-algebra sheaf $\mathcal O$, a fixed $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ and a strict derived tower $L_\bullet$. Write $H(K,-)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(K,-)$. The tensor-Hom identity of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], followed by [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], gives, for every $V\in D(\mathcal O)$ and derived product $P=\prod_n^D L_n$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(V,H(K,P))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V\otimes^L K,P)\cong\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(V\otimes^L K,L_n)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,\prod_n^D H(K,L_n)).$$
Thus the projection-defined map $H(K,P)\to\prod_n^D H(K,L_n)$ is an isomorphism. The same internal-Hom node gives exactness and shifts; [lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit], with $U$ final, says derived sections preserve these products and Roos triangles. These comparisons retain the $R$-actions: their underlying abelian-group comparisons are isomorphisms, so their cones have zero cohomology as $R$-modules. Consequently applying $F=R\Gamma(U,H(K,-))$ to the natural Roos triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] gives the Roos triangle of the strict mapping tower, since its product comparison intertwines $F(1-s)$ and $1-s'$. On the fixed functorial resolutions of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], the mapping-tower chain maps and their cone maps specify this comparison; the product isomorphisms make its third map an isomorphism. Hence
$$\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(K,R\lim L_\bullet)\cong R\lim_n\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(K,L_n).$$
All maps used are the projection and Hom-complex maps, so this comparison is natural in the strict derived tower and contravariantly in $K$. Products are derived products throughout.

proof.text: The coefficient ring $A_n$ is finite by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] and [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients]. At a fixed finite level, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] supplies a bounded constructible etale representative $K'_n$ of $K_n$. Use the dualizing-object identification of [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] and the compact-support identification of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Apply [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] on the ordinary etale site with $f=a$, $M=K'_n$, and target $(A_n)_s$, and then take derived global sections (the two composites are derived sections on $X$ and on $s$, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]). The point $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian because the only ideals of the field are $0$ and $k$. The finite-type morphism $a$ then has Noetherian source by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Since $s$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies a compactification of the separated finite-type morphism $a$. Its proper finite-type ambient scheme is also Noetherian by the same finite-type lemma. This gives the etale mapping-complex adjunction. The natural pullback map on mapping complexes is an isomorphism for bounded-below inputs: on degree $i$ cohomology it is the fully faithful Hom map for the inputs shifted by $i$, by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] and [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]. Thus it transports this actual mapping-complex adjunction to the pro-etale site. Sections at the coefficient point are exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], so their termwise and derived versions agree. Finally the finite coefficient-point equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] identifies the point mapping complex with ordinary module derived Hom (the evaluation comparison is an isomorphism on all shifted Hom groups). We obtain a natural isomorphism $\gamma_n:\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_n}(K_n,\omega_{X,n})\cong\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(C_n,A_n)$. All finite-site comparison inputs are bounded below; no unbounded pro-etale exceptional adjunction is used.

proof.text:
Check the transitions before taking a limit. Write $F_m=Ra_{!,m}$, $T_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$, and $c_{m,n}:T_{m,n}F_m\cong F_nT_{m,n}$. The morphism $u_{m,n}$ in step 1 satisfies, by [lem-coef-finite-dualizing],
$$\varepsilon_n F_n(u_{m,n})=T_{m,n}(\varepsilon_m)c_{m,n,\omega_m}^{-1}.$$
The mapping-complex map $\gamma_m$ of step 7 is induced by the evaluation/adjunction map followed by $\varepsilon_m$ of [prop-asd-internal-adjunction]. Let $H_m=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{X,A_m}(K_m,\omega_m)$. The left transition is the transpose of
$$H_m\otimes_R^L K_n\cong T_{m,n}(H_m\otimes_R^L K_m)\xrightarrow{T_{m,n}(\mathrm{ev})}T_{m,n}\omega_m\xrightarrow{u_{m,n}}\omega_n.$$
The right transition is the transpose of the composite $J_m\otimes_R^L C_n\cong T_{m,n}(J_m\otimes_R^L C_m)\xrightarrow{T_{m,n}(\mathrm{ev})}A_n$, where $J_m=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_m}(C_m,A_m)$. Transpose the square with these two evaluation maps and substitute the displayed counit identity. The compatibility with projection counits stated in [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change] applies here: $K_m$ has finite Tor amplitude by step 4, and $\omega_m$ does by step 3. For the evaluation tensor inputs one uses the canonical comparison map, rather than an uncited assertion of its invertibility. Naturality of $c$ moves $T_{m,n}(F_m(-))$ across $c^{-1}$; the resulting composite is precisely evaluation followed by $F_n(u_{m,n})$ and $\varepsilon_n$, hence the map defining $\gamma_n$ after the quotient transition. The extension-restriction comparisons proved in step 5 respect composition and evaluation, so the square commutes as a square of derived mapping complexes. The compact-support coefficient comparisons used on the right are the canonical ones of [lem-coef-integral-compact-support]; after sections their reductions are those of [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction]. This establishes the finite counit compatibility only in the evaluated derived categories. The actual tower morphism will be constructed in steps 9--11; no strict commutativity is inferred here from equality after localization.

proof.text:
First lift a single trace, independent of the variable $K$. Fix the compactification used in step 7. On its small ringed tower sites put $\mathcal Q_W(n,U)=(A_n)_W(U)$, with restriction in the index direction given by the quotient maps. A $\mathcal Q_W$-module is a strict inverse system of $(A_n)_W$-modules with semilinear transitions. This follows directly from the sheaf condition, which is imposed separately at each index, exactly as in [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. The complexes $Q_n$ of step 1 are such a module complex $Q_\bullet$. Apply extension by zero, derived proper direct image, and derived point sections on these tower sites, then forget to the constant base ring $R$; denote the resulting object by $B_\omega\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$. Under the ringed direct-image composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], forgetting the $\mathcal Q$-action commutes with these direct images: both composites are direct image along the same composite ringed-topos morphism. More explicitly, let $U_W$ be exact restriction from $\mathcal Q_W$-modules to modules over the tower-constant completed ring $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}$. For the proper map $p$, the equality of composite ringed-topos maps and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] give
$$U_s Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}\cong Rp_*^{R^{\mathrm{const}}}U_{\overline X}.$$
Here $RU_W=U_W$ because restriction is exact, by the kernel/cokernel argument of step 5. Evaluate the right side using [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison], which applies to towers over the fixed completed ring sheaf. At level $n$ apply the same ringed-composition statement to the scalar map $R_W\to(A_n)_W$; this identifies $Rp_*^{R_W}\operatorname{Res}_nQ_n$ with $\operatorname{Res}_n Rp_*^{A_n}Q_n$. This constructs the finite evaluation isomorphisms without asserting that evaluation of a K-injective $\mathcal Q$-module tower is K-injective: its prospective left adjoint uses nonexact quotient tensor. For open extension the scalar-forgetting comparison is the identity on its extension-by-zero presheaf. Now [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] supplies the evaluation identifications after restriction to completed coefficients; [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] identifies them with $\Gamma(s,F_n\omega_n)$. Thus the finite counits give maps $\epsilon_n:(B_\omega)_n\to A_n$ in $D(R)$. They commute with the transitions by the counit identity of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing]: transpose $u_{n+1,n}$ under scalar adjunction, apply compact support and its scalar-restriction comparison, and then compose with $\varepsilon_n$. The result is the quotient $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ after $\varepsilon_{n+1}$, since transposing the displayed counit identity is precisely this equality. This calculation involves only the dualizing tower.

Choose a strict complex $B_\bullet$ representing $B_\omega$ and a resolution $A_\bullet\to I_\bullet$ in the tower category, K-injective with injective terms, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the one-point ringed tower site. Each $I_n$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective]. Each degreewise transition $q:I_{n+1}^r\to I_n^r$ has an $R$-linear section: for an $R$-module $V$, let $T_n(V)$ be $V$ at indices $1,\ldots,n$, with identity transitions, and zero above. The inclusion $T_n(V)\hookrightarrow T_{n+1}(V)$ is monic; maps $T_n(V)\to I^r_\bullet$ are maps $V\to I_n^r$. Extend the map corresponding to $1_{I_n^r}$ by injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions] to obtain the asserted section.

By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], choose a chain map $e_1:B_1\to I_1$ representing $\epsilon_1$. Inductively, with $e_n$ fixed, choose $g:B_{n+1}\to I_{n+1}$ representing $\epsilon_{n+1}$. The finite counit identity says $qg-e_n b_n$ is zero after localization, where $b_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$ is the source transition. The same K-injective Hom bijection gives an actual degree-minus-one map $h:B_{n+1}\to I_n$ with $qg-e_nb_n=dh+hd$. Lift $h$ degreewise through the chosen graded section of $q$, obtaining $\widetilde h$. Set $e_{n+1}=g-d\widetilde h-\widetilde h d$. Then $e_{n+1}$ is a chain map homotopic to $g$, and $qe_{n+1}=e_nb_n$ as chain maps. Induction gives a strict tower map $e_\bullet:B_\bullet\to I_\bullet$. The roof
$$B_\bullet\xrightarrow{e_\bullet}I_\bullet\xleftarrow{\sim}A_\bullet$$
defines $t:B_\omega\to A_\bullet$ in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$ evaluating to every finite counit. Fix this trace once. No functorial choice of homotopies in $K$ is needed, since this construction has no $K$ in its data; no uniqueness of $t$ from its evaluations is asserted.

proof.text:
Construct the pairing on these actual ringed tower sites. Put $\mathsf H(K)=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(K,\operatorname{Res}Q_\bullet)\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$: take a K-injective tower resolution of $\operatorname{Res}Q_\bullet$, apply the ordinary global Hom complex from a fixed representative of $K$ at each index, and localize. To identify its relative evaluation map on the tower site, choose a K-flat $P\to K$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its constant diagram is K-flat: tensoring an acyclic diagram with it is acyclic at every index. The sheaf Hom on the tower site from this constant diagram to $I_\bullet$ is the termwise sheaf Hom $\mathcal Hom(P,I_n)$: over the slice at $(n,U)$ a compatible map from the constant first argument is determined by its component at $(n,U)$, with all lower components its restrictions. By [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective] this internal Hom is K-injective, so termwise sections compute its derived direct image to the point tower site. Its usual derived evaluation is therefore the evaluation of this very $\mathsf H(K)$, not of an independently chosen family of mapping complexes. Evaluation of the resolution is K-injective by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective]; hence [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] identifies its $n$-th evaluation with $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{R_X}(K,\operatorname{Res}_n\omega_n)$. A quasi-isomorphism in $K$ gives quasi-isomorphisms at every index, so this construction descends contravariantly to the derived category. This is a functor with values in the derived tower category, not only a tower of functors to $D(R)$.

Let $\mathsf K_\bullet$ be derived extension of the constant $K$-diagram along the ring map $R_X\to\mathcal Q_X$ on the tower site. A K-flat representative $P\to K$ gives the strict representative $P\otimes_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ with its quotient chain maps; it evaluates to $K_n$. K-flat diagram replacements and their localization are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Let $B_K$ be compact support and point sections of $\mathsf K_\bullet$, computed on the same diagram sites. It is the tower lift $\mathcal T_a^c K$ of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor] followed by point sections: both use this K-flat reduction diagram, the same open extension, and separately derived proper direct image; [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies their composites before evaluation.

Write $\mathscr T_R$ for the point tower site with constant ring $R$, and write $v_W^R:(W_{\mathrm{proet}}\times\mathbf N,R_W^{\mathrm{const}})\to\mathscr T_R$, where $R_W^{\mathrm{const}}$ denotes the diagram constant in the index with value the completed sheaf $R_W$. There is also $v_W^{\mathcal Q}:(W_{\mathrm{proet}}\times\mathbf N,\mathcal Q_W)\to\mathscr T_R$, using the quotient scalar maps. Here $\mathbf N$ is indexed from $1$. The first paragraph realizes $\mathsf H(K)$ as the derived direct image of the relative Hom over $R_X^{\mathrm{const}}$. Its evaluation is therefore the counit/evaluation composite
$$L(v_X^R)^*\mathsf H(K)\otimes^L_{R_X^{\mathrm{const}}}\operatorname{const}K\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}Q_\bullet.$$
Extend scalars along $R_X^{\mathrm{const}}\to\mathcal Q_X$ and apply scalar adjunction to its target. The resulting actual tower-site morphism is
$$L(v_X^{\mathcal Q})^*\mathsf H(K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal Q_X}\mathsf K_\bullet\longrightarrow Q_\bullet.$$
The tensor reassociation here is the map $(h\otimes a)\otimes(p\otimes b)\mapsto(h\otimes p)\otimes ab$ on K-flat representatives, with inverse $(h\otimes p)\otimes a\mapsto(h\otimes1)\otimes(p\otimes a)$; it respects the differentials and quotient transitions. Thus this scalar change is made on the diagram site before evaluation. Here evaluation is the Hom-complex evaluation on the chosen representatives, and its derived form is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction, lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]; scalar extension is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and the adjunction is step 5 applied on this small ringed site. For completeness, let $g_s:(s_{\mathrm{proet}}\times\mathbf N,\mathcal Q_s)\to\mathscr T_R$ be point sections and put $V=L g_s^*\mathsf H(K)$. In the proper projection morphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] use the pullback of this $V$ to the compactification. After compact support, use the projection morphism for $g_s$ itself, with input $\mathsf H(K)\in D(\mathscr T_R)$. This gives the composite
$$\mathsf H(K)\otimes_R^L Rg_{s,*}F^{\mathcal Q}\mathsf K_\bullet\longrightarrow Rg_{s,*}(V\otimes_{\mathcal Q_s}^L F^{\mathcal Q}\mathsf K_\bullet)\longrightarrow Rg_{s,*}F^{\mathcal Q}(L(v_X^{\mathcal Q})^*\mathsf H(K)\otimes_{\mathcal Q_X}^L\mathsf K_\bullet)\longrightarrow Rg_{s,*}F^{\mathcal Q}Q_\bullet.$$
Here $F^{\mathcal Q}=Rp_*^{\mathcal Q}j_!$ is separately derived compact support on the quotient-ring tower sites. The first and second arrows are the specified projection morphisms (and the open tensor identification below), and the third is the just constructed evaluation map. Restriction to $\mathscr T_R$ identifies the source and target with $\mathsf H(K)\otimes_R^L B_K$ and $B_\omega$ by the ringed direct-image compositions already used. In particular the proper projection formula is applied to $\mathcal Q$-modules, while its final point-sections application has base ring $R$. For open extension use the natural tensor identification $V\otimes j_!P=j_!(j^*V\otimes P)$: before sheafification both sides are the same tensor module on objects factoring through the open and zero otherwise; sheafification and tensor are left adjoints, so the identification descends, and K-flat representatives give its derived version. The exact open adjunction is [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. We obtain
$$\beta_K:\mathsf H(K)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B_K\longrightarrow B_\omega$$
as a morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$. The tensor here is the derived pointwise tensor, constructed on the point ringed tower site. This only uses the ambient projection MORPHISM; no assertion that its evaluation tensor input is constructible or has finite Tor dimension, and no invertibility of that morphism, is needed. Its evaluated maps are projection followed by evaluation, because the projection map is the adjunct of pullback tensor followed by the proper counit. These are maps already formed on the diagram sites, so no lifting of a family of localized squares is being asserted. Naturality of tensor, evaluation and the projection morphism gives the evaluation dinaturality identity for $K\to K'$ as an identity of diagram-category morphisms.

proof.text:
There is a natural coaugmentation $\operatorname{const}C\to B_K$ in the derived tower category. Indeed [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] defines $Ra_!K$ as the derived limit of its compact-support reduction tower. Derived point sections commute with this limit by [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison], so $C\cong R\lim B_K$. On a K-injective tower representative $J_\bullet$ for $B_K$, the compatible-sequence inclusions $\operatorname{const}(\lim J_n)\to J_\bullet$ are an actual chain map of towers; its derived class is the required coaugmentation. This construction respects maps of K-injective towers and chain homotopies, hence is natural on their derived category by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Its evaluations are the quotient maps $C\to C_n$ under the canonical comparisons of step 4; their adjuncts $C\otimes_R^LA_n\to C_n$ are isomorphisms.

Compose, in the derived tower category,
$$\mathsf H(K)\otimes_R^L\operatorname{const}C\longrightarrow\mathsf H(K)\otimes_R^LB_K\xrightarrow{\beta_K}B_\omega\xrightarrow{t}A_\bullet.$$
Currying gives an actual morphism
$$\Gamma_K:\mathsf H(K)\longrightarrow\mathsf J(C):=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_\bullet)$$
in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$. This currying is the tensor-Hom adjunction on the point ringed tower site [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction, lem-pur-rhom-global-sections]; a constant K-flat representative of $C$ and a K-injective tower representative of $A_\bullet$ compute its target by the termwise Hom complexes. Evaluation is therefore $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_n)$. The evaluated composite defining $\Gamma_K$ is projection, evaluation, the finite counit, and the map $C\to C_n$. By steps 5, 7 and 8 it is exactly $\gamma_n$ followed by the scalar-adjunction isomorphism $\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(C_n,A_n)\cong\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_n)$. Every evaluation is thus an isomorphism. The cone of $\Gamma_K$ has acyclic evaluations, so is acyclic as a tower complex, since exactness is levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]; hence $\Gamma_K$ is an isomorphism in the derived tower category. Finally, for $K\to K'$ the dinaturality identity for $\beta$, naturality of the coaugmentation, and the single fixed trace $t$ give the currying identity $\mathsf J(C\to C')\Gamma_{K'}=\Gamma_K\mathsf H(K\to K')$. Thus $\Gamma_K$ is natural contravariantly in $K$ before taking limits. No K-dependent rectification, or faithfulness of evaluation on derived morphisms, is used.

proof.text:
Apply step 6 to the particular strict dualizing tower of steps 1--2 and its mapping-tower functor $\mathsf H(K)$ of step 10. This gives
$$\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,\omega_{X,R})\cong R\lim\mathsf H(K).$$
Here $R\lim$ is the total derived inverse-limit functor on $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The construction of $\mathsf H(K)$ uses a K-injective tower resolution of this very dualizing tower, so the projection maps are those of step 6. In particular no independent strict realization of the finite mapping complexes is substituted. Step 5 identifies its evaluations with the left finite mapping complexes used to recognize $\Gamma_K$ in step 11.

proof.text:
The right tower is the specific object $\mathsf J(C)=\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_\bullet)$ constructed in step 11, rather than a new realization of its evaluated finite Hom complexes. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $R$ is a DVR with finite residue field and $0<|\varpi|_E<1$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete], $E$ is complete for its extending absolute value. If $(\bar x_n)_n$ is a compatible system in $A_n$, choose representatives $x_n\in R$; for $m\ge n$ one has $|x_m-x_n|_E\le|\varpi|_E^n$. Thus $(x_n)$ is Cauchy, its limit $x$ lies in the closed unit ball $R$, and $x-x_n\in\varpi^n R$ by the same norm bound. Uniqueness follows from $|x-y|_E\le|\varpi|_E^n$ for every $n$. This proves $R\cong\varprojlim_n A_n$. The quotient transitions are surjective by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients]. In the category of modules the two-term product map $1-s$ is surjective (for a prescribed $(b_n)$ choose $x_1=0$ and lift $x_n-b_n$ to $x_{n+1}$ along $A_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_n$; then $x_n-q_{n+1,n}(x_{n+1})=b_n$), with kernel $R$, so its Roos complex is quasi-isomorphic to $R[0]$. Consequently $R\lim_n A_n\cong R$. Applying step 6 on the one-object trivial site, with $\mathcal O=R$, first argument $C$, and tower $L_n=A_n$ with its quotient transitions, gives
$$R\lim\mathsf J(C)\cong R\lim_n\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,A_n)\cong\mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,R).$$
No inverse-limit/cohomology interchange occurs.

proof.text: The tower morphism $\Gamma_K:\mathsf H(K)\to\mathsf J(C)$ constructed in step 11 is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))$. Apply the exact functor $R\lim:D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R)))\to D(R)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. It gives a canonical isomorphism $R\lim\mathsf H(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim\mathsf J(C)$, which is the derived-limit image of the tower morphism rather than an inference from unrelated levelwise isomorphisms. Compose this map with the identifications of steps 12 and 13 to obtain the asserted natural isomorphism of mapping complexes. Taking $H^0$ uses [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on $X$. At the coefficient point, $Ra_!K$ and $R_s$ are constructible (the latter by [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]); [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence] identifies their Hom group with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(R)}(C,R)$. Hence $\omega_{X,R}$ represents the right-adjoint value at $R_s$, and representing objects with their natural bijections are unique up to the unique isomorphism preserving those bijections. This is the canonical meaning of the object and adjunction claimed here; arbitrary choices of unrelated Roos cones have not been declared canonical. Explicitly, the two representation bijections send the identity of each representing object to maps in the two directions; naturality says their composites correspond to the identities, so the bijections force both composites to be identities.
